note: Attribution problem is the central finding. The ImportKey 'bhakti-enterprises' page does show dated export rows with destination, HS code and B/L numbers (e.g. 2026-02-25 to St Petersburg, HS 84439100, B/L 1010059; 2026-02-20 to Lima, HS 84439100, B/L 9857715; 2026-02-19 to Kuala Lumpur, HS 84212900, B/L 9825533; 2026-02-18 to Vilnius, HS 84439100, B/L 9785226), but (1) the exact-name variant 'BHAKTI ENTERPRISES PRAVIN DIPCHAND DOSHI' returns zero records, (2) the address is a shared multi-tenant Mumbai trading address, and (3) the row set mixes photocopier consumables with polyester woven fabric, which no single IT/electronics trader would ship. Declared HS codes 844331/844332/847130/851762 (copiers, printers, laptops, network gear) do NOT match the observed 84439100 (parts of printing machinery) or 84212900 (filtering machinery) — the observed codes are parts/accessories, not the declared finished machines. Per project rules this is not a rejection ground; the record is kept and the HS should be corrected to the observed 84439100 / 84212900. Verdict on shipments: export activity is visible in customs data but cannot be tied to this legal entity with confidence, so it is recorded as declared_only rather than confirmed. No domestic supply traces found; revenue and export volume: null (not public). Recommend obtaining the actual IEC and matching it against the customs records before treating any of these B/Ls as this supplier's.
